decisions.title: Autonomous agent option C with tools and durable memory
decisions.context: Owner explicitly chose option C; practical tasks are primary, not avatar realism.
decisions.decision: Keep core task orchestration and memory first.

decisions.title: Single-user modular monolith on Windows
decisions.context: Lower operational cost than microservices for one host and user. Baseline adopted for initial implementation; future changes require superseding ADR and compatible migration.
decisions.decision: Python application with clean ports; workers logical.
decisions.revisit_when: Multiple independent users or remote deployment needs arise.

decisions.title: SQLite with FTS5 as initial durable store
decisions.context: Local low-administration default with versioned migrations. Baseline adopted for initial implementation; future changes require superseding ADR and compatible migration.
decisions.decision: Use abstraction for semantic index and potential PostgreSQL replacement.
decisions.revisit_when: Concurrency, scale or retrieval benchmark fails.

decisions.title: LLM/provider-agnostic identity and model router
decisions.context: Preserve user continuity across local and cloud models. Baseline adopted for initial implementation; future changes require superseding ADR and compatible migration.
decisions.decision: Never store identity or task truth in model weights alone.
decisions.revisit_when: No provider-independent evaluation succeeds.

decisions.title: Local by default; cloud explicit opt-in
decisions.context: Respects privacy and offline utility without giving up quality. Baseline adopted for initial implementation; future changes require superseding ADR and compatible migration.
decisions.decision: Cloud is gated and task-sensitive.
decisions.revisit_when: Owner supplies different data transfer constraints.

decisions.title: Tool registry and authorization before execution
decisions.context: Action correctness and side-effect safety cannot be delegated to LLM. Baseline adopted for initial implementation; future changes require superseding ADR and compatible migration.
decisions.decision: Typed tools, policy gates, audit and verifier.
decisions.revisit_when: Security review finds stronger isolation needed.

decisions.title: Versioned facts/events and project-scoped retrieval
decisions.context: Source lineage and contradictory decisions must remain inspectable. Baseline adopted for initial implementation; future changes require superseding ADR and compatible migration.
decisions.decision: Store provenance and supersession, not overwrite summaries.
decisions.revisit_when: Storage benchmark or privacy requirement changes.

decisions.title: Controlled skill evolution; no autonomous core changes
decisions.context: Useful improvement without uncontrolled code execution.
decisions.decision: Sandbox proposals, tests, owner promotion.
decisions.revisit_when: Owner approves alternative governance mechanism.

decisions.title: No automatic weight fine-tuning in initial releases
decisions.context: Insufficient curated examples and benchmark at project start.
decisions.decision: Retain data selection/evaluation possibility later.
decisions.revisit_when: Sufficient training data and success metric exist.

decisions.title: Browser via Playwright where suitable; MCP optional
decisions.context: Browser automation needs deterministic safety and observation.
decisions.decision: Treat MCP as adapter, not central dependency.
decisions.revisit_when: Browser/tool benchmarks demand other implementation.

decisions.title: Telegram bot before personal-account integration
decisions.context: Separate channel simpler to secure, test and audit.
decisions.decision: Stage personal-account integration later.
decisions.revisit_when: Owner changes integration priorities.

decisions.title: JSON canonical specs, Markdown explanatory documents
decisions.context: Stable IDs, easy AI indexing and stdlib validation. Baseline adopted for initial implementation; future changes require superseding ADR and compatible migration.
decisions.decision: Keep schemas and traceability authoritative.
decisions.revisit_when: Schema complexity warrants another IDL.

decisions.title: No default multi-agent orchestration
decisions.context: One orchestrator and bounded tools simpler to debug and evaluate.
decisions.decision: Multi-agent only after measured benefit.
decisions.revisit_when: Parallel benchmark demonstrates advantage.

decisions.title: Conservative action approvals and no automatic external sends
decisions.context: Avoid unapproved communication, purchases and OS changes. Baseline adopted for initial implementation; future changes require superseding ADR and compatible migration.
decisions.decision: Approval bound to concrete effect/recipient/target.
decisions.revisit_when: Owner refines authorization rules.

decisions.title: Select Qwen3.5 9B as default local model, without comparative model testing
decisions.context: Owner explicitly selected Qwen3.5 9B for the initial agent and declined model comparison tests. This selects a planned implementation default, not an installed runtime.
decisions.decision: Use Ollama tag qwen3.5:9b by default. Implement only this local model first. Retain provider-neutral contracts but do not schedule A/B model benchmarks, alternatives or model-ranking as release prerequisites. Retain minimal startup smoke checks, functional verification and security tests.
decisions.revisit_when: Owner explicitly changes model choice or later requests evaluations.

decisions.title: Store assistant and runtime state in portable G-drive home
decisions.context: Owner requests one dedicated G: directory containing project code, local model, history, memory and supporting files for migration and management.
decisions.decision: Use G:\Assistant as default home. Repo in repo/, Ollama models in models/ollama, durable data in data/{db,history,memory,identity,skills}, work in workspace/, logs, backups and cache separated. Resolve paths through ASSISTANT_ROOT; OLLAMA_MODELS for Ollama. Never silently fall back to C:. Keep secrets and runtime data out of Git, protect backups and validate restoration.
decisions.revisit_when: Owner changes storage or destination disk.

decisions.title: Trusted action classification by exact operation and target
decisions.context: An LLM cannot assign its own privileges, and an integration like GitHub supports both read and externally mutating calls.
decisions.decision: The trusted registry determines side-effect class, operation identity, resource scope and sensitivity from validated arguments; ToolRequest contains only intent, never authoritative risk class. Separate read and write capabilities; externally mutating GitHub actions require approval. Default deny on ambiguity.
decisions.revisit_when: Owner approves new bounded policy after threat review.

decisions.title: Minimal safe idempotent task recovery in M1
decisions.context: M1 acceptance SCN-005 requires restart-safe state, while original advanced scheduler task was M3.
decisions.decision: M1 must persist intent, step/action IDs, approval and pre/post side-effect journal, expose blocked/needs_reconciliation, and refuse automatic replay of uncertain effects; M3 implements advanced scheduling and connector-specific reconciliation.

decisions.title: Architecture baseline v1 gate and contract coverage
decisions.context: A coding agent can omit untracked requirements or trust syntactically valid but structurally invalid JSON.
decisions.decision: Every non-deprecated requirement has an implementation or explicitly deferred task and acceptance evidence; enforce relationship in CI. Validate schema fixtures with JSON Schema 2020-12 and run on Windows and Linux. Functional safety checks remain mandatory; do not compare LLM alternatives.
decisions.revisit_when: Owner changes development process or validation policy.

decisions.title: Windows primary; Linux create-only tools in trusted environment
decisions.context: Unprivileged Linux directory descriptors do not prohibit another owner process from renaming the authority root. Windows can pin the ancestor handle chain.
decisions.decision: Keep Windows the primary target. On Linux trust the application and project-root anchors and allow only flat new-file names directly in the project root. Deny nested create paths before dispatch to avoid in-project directory rename races. Require no-follow handle traversal, O_TMPFILE, exclusive publication and Landlock ABI 3+. Fail closed when mechanisms are unavailable. Never claim isolation from malicious same-account root relocation.
decisions.revisit_when: Linux needs hostile-root isolation or a different filesystem/OS backend; requires a reviewed design, not a pathname fallback.

decisions.title: Explicit partial analysis and bounded references for M1 review remediation
decisions.owner: project owner via requested bounded-context fixes and honest semantic outcomes
decisions.context: The 32 KiB tool limit exceeds the 6000-byte LLM message envelope. Copying full evidence/plans into final prompts can deadlock already verified actions.
decisions.decision: Extend ADR-018 task lifecycle with terminal partial when complete source analysis is unavailable; retain all verified evidence and emit CLI exit 2. Keep complete saved results and requests separate from bounded LLM projections. Append revisions bind the exact saved base digest and retain old steps in trusted code. SQLite v3 adds preview ownership/expiry inventory and gates older binaries; no action/approval rewrite.
decisions.revisit_when: A reviewed chunked full-analysis workflow or a new context budget is authorized.
decisions.migration: Back up v1/v2 before opening with v3. Transactional additive migration preserves IDs, digests, approvals and evidence. Restore matching backup and older code to roll back; do not downgrade user_version manually.

decisions.title: M1 scoped data admission and closed diagnostics
decisions.owner: project owner via requested M1 security implementation
decisions.context: Explicit implementation request for source/policy separation, data classification, secret boundaries and honest unchanged P0 acceptance.
decisions.decision: Refine ADR-006/017 without changing the baseline: owner-controlled whole-file and memory labels, exact private local-context grants, recursive known-credential denial at runtime sinks, minimal child environment and closed diagnostic codes. Keep opaque or misclassified secrets and unimplemented connectors as unmet P0 acceptance, not lowered requirements.
decisions.migration: SQLite remains v3; no stored content/approvals rewritten. Legacy exact file scope retains internal local-context meaning. New private labels are owner grants; old binaries do not enforce them and are not an approved privacy rollback.
decisions.revisit_when: Owner approves an authoritative secret inventory/vault, stricter data-admission protocol or explicit acceptance revision after reviewing residual risks.

decisions.title: Fail-closed file alias policy for M1 scopes
decisions.owner: project owner via explicit PR #6 alias remediation request
decisions.context: Case-sensitive scope strings can classify one Windows file inconsistently.
decisions.decision: Refine ADR-006/017/023: reject duplicate/colliding grants, require exact Windows opened long names and known case-insensitive directory policy, retain single-link and physical-identity checks. Revalidate legacy scopes before model/tool dispatch and again in workers. No permission normalization or fallback. Linux keeps ADR-021 exact-name trusted-root flat-create semantics. See docs/engineering/m1-file-aliases.md
decisions.migration: SQLite stays v3; do not rewrite grants, approvals, action IDs or evidence. Ambiguous legacy scopes block; owner reviews exact long names and creates a new task. Uncertain effects remain needs_reconciliation. Noncanonical roots and unsupported directory case queries fail closed.
decisions.revisit_when: A reviewed backend supports additional filesystems, Windows case-sensitive directories or alternative alias bindings.

decisions.title: Proposed bounded M1 trust/data acceptance and per-connector gates
decisions.owner: proposed for explicit project owner decision
decisions.context: Literal REQ-017 includes absent connectors; universal REQ-019 cannot be proven for unknown or misclassified arbitrary contents.
decisions.decision: Recommend option B in docs/engineering/m1-trust-boundary-proposal.md: enumerated M1 ingress/sinks, owner classification, reviewed secret inventory/vault, default-deny, fail-closed, and mandatory actual-adapter gates at M2-M4. TASK-049 implements bounded inventory/admission/legacy review with a disabled vault port under the explicit implementation request. Acceptance approval is still pending in spec/owner-decisions-adr025.json. This proposal changes no requirement text, priority, milestone or status; M1 and original P0 acceptance stay open.
decisions.migration: Only after recorded owner approval: explicitly revise acceptance and traceability, implement agreed missing controls, review legacy data without automatic erasure/relabeling, rerun Windows/Ubuntu and selected-Qwen host evidence. No deployment or merge implied.
decisions.revisit_when: Owner answers the three explicit questions in the proposal.

decisions.title: Owner-authorized M1 metadata inventory and fail-closed legacy admission
decisions.owner: project owner via explicit bounded M1 implementation request
decisions.context: Owner authorized implementation of option B controls while explicitly withholding acceptance/status changes pending three ADR-025 decisions.
decisions.decision: Refine ADR-023/024 source admission: new owner APIs attest whole datasets; old sources require ID/hash review, with no implicit internal legacy labels. Add metadata-only inventory, private local sink grants and disabled Windows Credential Manager interface. Preserve all authority/effect/reconciliation/alias invariants. ADR-025 remains provisional and REQ-017/019 unchanged.
decisions.migration: SQLite v4 adds data_admissions, sensitive_inventory, data_reviews only. Automatic consistent verified backup before v1-v3 upgrade; transaction rollback; no source, scope, result or approval rewrite or attestation during migration. Restore matching backup/code for rollback under separate owner approval. See docs/engineering/m1-trust-inventory.md.
decisions.revisit_when: Owner explicitly decides ADR-025 acceptance, enables a separately verified connector, or changes trust assumptions.

decisions.title: Owner-bound reconciliation, admission renewal and derived memory index consistency
decisions.owner: project owner via explicit PR #8 targeted remediation request
decisions.context: Independent review 5722142390 found stale reconciliation receipts, missing FTS restoration and a durable-memory authorization renewal gap.
decisions.decision: Refine ADR-026 without changing acceptance: validate project/current digest/admission before atomic owner reconciliation and receipt refresh; preserve expiry and all effect authority. Review/renew synchronizes only exact eligible memory FTS entries. Explicit owner renewal binds unchanged ID/project/digest/class/expiry, appends receipt history, and rechecks inventory/scope. Canonical retention is independent of 30-day projection authorization; bounded payload-free historical audit survives expiry. ADR-025 remains provisional and REQ-017/019 unchanged.
decisions.migration: SQLite remains v4; use existing data_reviews for append-only prior/new receipt metadata. No migration or source/grant/approval rewrite. Previously stale reconciled tasks require independent explicit review. Matching backup/code rollback remains owner-gated; see m1-trust-inventory.md.
decisions.revisit_when: Owner changes renewal lifetime, archive access, trust assumptions or accepts ADR-025 separately.
